options.npc_answer: I just escaped with: [inventory_list]. You look like you've seen better days too. See, I have some good stuff here if you needed.

options.player_question: Where did the name Pox come from?
options.npc_answer: Black dots first, then the bleeding. Some doc said 'the Pox' on live TV, and the name stuck better than the cure.
Gone? No. It's still there. It's just not ours anymore.
Trade, Information, Passage. Or as we say here: Try, Improvise, Pray.
The good bunkers have food. The rest have a door and a smell.
Cheap land, deep water, no neighbours. Rich people plan for taxes, not plagues.
Money with legs. They bought the rocks we're standing on, then bet them on a cure.
Two labs racing the same r-pox. Parallel research, they call it. Parallel panic, I call it.

options.player_question: Is r-pox the same as the Pox?
options.npc_answer: The Pox, the r-pox, the rot. Same thing wearing different hats.
Half the frequencies lie, the other half scream. Learn the difference and you'll live a week longer.
You need rank, a code, or a very patient friend with a soldering iron.
Boats, dead sailors, and one guy in a shack who draws maps from memory. Take your pick.
Fuel, fear, and the horde on the dock. In that order.
Millions of sweating bodies, one virus. It was a party the Pox never left.
On paper. Beautiful paper. Three days later Rio was smoke and sirens.
First the dots. Then the bleeding. Then the quiet. The quiet is the worst part.
A mountain range under the water. The rich bought the peaks. Now the peaks are islands.
Sand shores everywhere. Safe ones? That's a different question.
Find wheels. Anything with wheels. A cart is a vehicle if you believe hard enough.
Caves are dark, dry, and quiet. Two of those are good.
Follow the chatter. If the chatter stops, don't follow anymore.

options.player_question: Can you get me to the boat?
options.npc_answer: If you get me to the boat, we both win. That's the whole deal.
Infected, armed, and dancing their last dance. Stay out of the dance.

options.player_question: Why don't rotters attack the infected?
options.npc_answer: They smell their own. That's why some people wear the smell. Camouflage, until it isn't.
Smart until you die of it. Then it's just a coffin you walk around in.
Quarantined, sealed, and forgotten. We're a footnote in the middle of the Atlantic.
Lost implies someone's looking. We're misplaced.

options.player_question: How big is the archipelago really?
options.npc_answer: Big enough that nobody agrees on the count. Small enough that everyone hears the same gunshots.
Blackout. Locked out. A heli, then gunshots. Then nothing but static.
We hear them. Faint, but alive. Faint is enough.
They sent one. Port's the meeting point. The horde's the problem.
BNews says a lot. BNews also says stay calm, which tells you how bad it is.
Stay indoors, stay quiet. The horde follows noise, and the noise follows you.
Half rations today, full stomach tomorrow. Maybe.
Then you wait for the next horde. That's the job now.
I believe in saying it out loud. Keeps the hands steady.
The static, maybe. It's the only thing that answers.
Water. You die in days without it, weeks with an empty stomach.
Boil it. If you can't boil it, pray over it. Same result, better mood.

options.player_question: What do the dots look like?
options.npc_answer: Small, black, polite. They don't hurt at first. That's the trick.
Hours. Sometimes less. Don't share a room with a maybe.
I trust the static between the news. That's where the truth hides.
Exxoil says maybe. Gethulius says maybe louder. Nobody says yes.
They work until they don't. Long exposure and you're just a volunteer with a bandage.
Nobody's calm. We're just tired of screaming.

options.player_question: What's the worst sound out here?
options.npc_answer: A radio that goes quiet mid-sentence.
A boat engine you didn't expect.
You can. The question is what swims with you.
Sharks are honest. Rotters lie about being dead.
Plenty. Half sell maps, half sell the same map twice.
Bullets, batteries, bandages, and gossip. Gossip is the cheapest and worth the most.
High, dry, one entrance. Three things. Get all three and sleep.
Rotters can't open doors, but they can lean on them until you're stupid.
Cold and alive beats warm and surrounded.
The radio is the only thing worth fixing.

options.player_question: How do I call for help?
options.npc_answer: Say your location, say your name, say it three times. Then listen.
Keep talking anyway. Somebody's always listening, even if they're scared.
Everybody heard them. The question is who was shooting.
Some are still soldiers. Some are just people with a uniform and a gun.

options.player_question: Where's the government in all this?
options.npc_answer: There's a government somewhere. It sends memos. The memos are very brave.
That's what the Council said about the whole archipelago. Then they charged us for the meeting.
Betting a lot on resources. The resources were not consulted.
Because sharing means admitting the other lab might win.
Labs leak, fences get taller, reports get shorter.
Depends who you ask. The people who said no are quiet now.
Animals carry everything. That's what animals do.
They remember doors. They remember the sound of a car.
Some shuffle. Some sprint. The sprinters are new and I hate them.
Yes. They adapt faster than us. It's the adults who keep dying of hope.
Noise. Real noise. Crowds, traffic, someone arguing about football.
On the radio, sometimes. Then the scores get weird because half the teams are gone.
Someone we used up. They're turning rogue now. Turns out people don't like being a resource.
Infected who stopped taking orders. The worst kind of employee.
Trust them with directions. Not with your boat.
Three. Don't lie about bites. Don't waste water. Don't promise a rescue you can't make.
Tell someone. Then decide what kind of person you want to be at the end.

options.player_question: Is there a cure in the caves?
options.npc_answer: There's a story about a cure in the caves. Stories are free and worth exactly that.

options.player_question: Why do people go to the bunkers?
options.npc_answer: Because a locked door feels like a plan.
Sometimes. Sometimes they answer and you wish they hadn't.
Far enough that nobody swims home.

options.player_question: Is the quarantine line still up?
options.npc_answer: The line is up. The people behind it aren't.
One, once. It flew over and didn't turn around.
The heli at GTH-42 started this mess. I don't trust anything with rotors now.
Fishing, hiding, and arguing about whose rock it is.
Fish don't care about the Pox. Cook them anyway.
All the water in the world and not a drop to drink.
Small jobs. Clean the radio, count the cans, patch the boat. Sanity is a chore list.
I sleep at dawn. Nights belong to the horde now.
Lighting a fire on a beach because you felt lonely.
Learning to shut up.

options.player_question: Why does the static sound like voices?
options.npc_answer: Because you want it to. That's how the Pox gets you — through your own ears.
Only when it's the last thing you hear before the gunshots.
We all heard. The boat heard too. That's why it left early.
If you can hear this, go to the port. Quiet. Now.

options.player_question: Will they come back for us?
options.npc_answer: They came once. That's more than most islands get.
Wave. Then start walking. Then start planning.
Worth is a rich man's word. Ask if it's survivable.
Hope is a ration. Spend it slow.
Names get people killed out here. Call me the voice on the radio.
I'll remember your call sign. That's the closest thing to a grave we have.
Keep strong, survivor. We will rebuild — after the horde passes, after the static clears, after the boat.
